about: The games played for vibration with a DualSense or DualSense Edge on a Mac. A game is added after a session, from what was felt and what the Wine modules logged, never from what it should do. Each test names its controller and its connection. docs/vibration.md is made from this file by tools/vibration-md.py.
stack: MacGameFix's Wine modules in a NotProton runner (CrossOver Preview 27), Steam Input off for the game, unless a result says otherwise.

results.not-recorded: Played; how it felt was not recorded

games.name: Marvel's Spider-Man 2
games.technology: Its own DualSense support, over raw HID. It plays its haptics as audio on the pad's audio output, which it finds by the audio endpoint's container.
games.description: Insomniac's PC port drives the pad itself, as on a PS5: haptics on the actuators and adaptive triggers, on a cable and over Bluetooth.
games.settings: Suggested: full motor power on the Edge and the Edge's haptics at 2x, on a cable and over Bluetooth.
details: It claims the motor power at 0x00 in every report for a standard DualSense, never for an Edge, which keeps its own stored reduction. With the power at full and the haptics at 2x the Edge felt like a standard DualSense.
It sends the same haptic signal to both pads (a level meter showed the same peaks and RMS for the same moments).
It reads feature reports 0x09, 0x20 and 0x05 only.
The touchpad moved the in-game camera (2026-10-20).

tests.notes: The same as on a cable.
The same as on a cable at 1x.

games.name: Mortal Kombat 1
games.technology: SDL 2 (SDL2.dll 2.32.0), which drives the pad over HID: the rumble as the pad's emulation of motors.
games.description: Each rumble ends with its hit, on a cable and over Bluetooth, since the Wine modules of 2026-10-20.
games.settings: Rumble on the haptic actuators is optional over Bluetooth.
details: SDL 2 asks an Edge (firmware 0x0217) for the old emulation at half strength and a DualSense from firmware 2.24 for the improved one at full; the modules give the Edge the improved one at twice what SDL wrote, as SDL 3 would.
SDL ends a rumble with a report that has no rumble bit; over Bluetooth the modules missed it until 2026-10-20, and the rumble went on for the whole fight.

tests.notes: 17 rumbles in 74 s, the motors on 6 % of the time, each ended by SDL's stop.
15 rumbles in 38 s, about 250 ms each.
34 rumbles in 73 s, none longer than 239 ms.

details: With Bluetooth as a cable on (the default), the modules logged trigger effects and motor values always at 0, and no haptics output opened (2026-10-21).
It vibrated the same way on NotProton's direct mode, without an audio output (2026-10-16).
Not played on a cable with the modules yet.

games.name: Nioh 3
games.technology: Its own DualSense support, over raw HID. It finds the pad's audio output through SetupAPI (the pad's container, SPDRP_BASE_CONTAINERID, against the audio render interfaces) and plays its haptics there through an XAudio2 mastering voice opened on that interface's path.
games.description: Haptics over Bluetooth, "vibrated very well", with three Wine module patches that are not released yet (0009, 0010, 0011) and the Edge shown as a standard DualSense with XInput off. Without the patches it finds no output and never vibrates, in Immersive or Functional mode.
games.settings: Game Feel: the Edge shown as a DualSense, XInput off. In the game: vibration mode Immersive.
details: 0009 lists Wine's audio outputs as SetupAPI interfaces with their containers; 0010 returns SPDRP_BASE_CONTAINERID as a WCHAR string from the A function, as Windows does; with both the game finds the pad's output.
It then creates an XAudio2 mastering voice with that output's path as its device id; 0011 makes XAudio2 open that device (Wine ignored the id and used the default output).
With the Edge shown as an Edge, or with XInput's rumble on the motors (the pad's id gains "&Col01"), it found the output and never created the voice.
The modules logged the haptics output opened on the Bluetooth pad, peaks up to 1.12, the queue at about 29 ms and nothing dropped.
In Functional mode, and without the patches, it never sends a motor value: a game that sees a DualSense plays only haptics.
Proton on Linux shows the same failure without these pieces: the triggers work and the haptic vibration does not (ValveSoftware/Proton#9473).

tests.notes: Patches 0009-0011, XInput off, Immersive: "vibrated very well".

games.name: NINJA GAIDEN 4
games.technology: Its own pad code over raw HID (its executable is encrypted; its imports match Nioh 3's), plus XInput and DirectInput.
games.description: Its own DualSense code drives the pad's motors, once it is shown a standard DualSense and the pad is a single HID device. With the Edge shown as an Edge, or with XInput's rumble on the motors (which adds a collection, so the pad's id gains "&Col01"), its code does not take the pad: no controller at all.
games.settings: Game Feel: the Edge shown as a DualSense, XInput off. Steam Input off.
details: With the defaults, and with the Edge shown as a DualSense but XInput's rumble on the motors, the game read the pad's reports 0x09, 0x20 and 0x05 and asked once for the old rumble emulation with both motors at 0, and the controller did nothing.
As an XInput controller it played, with Xbox prompts, and did not vibrate.
With the Edge shown as a DualSense and XInput off, the modules logged the game rumbling the pad's motors through its own code.

With Bluetooth as a cable off too, the controller did not work: the game read the pad's report 0x05, which switches a Bluetooth DualSense to its full report, and the modules saw nothing from it afterwards.

tests.notes: XInput off: controls and vibration.

games.name: Mortal Kombat 11
games.technology: NetherRealm's engine (the PC port by QLOC). It reads the pad through DirectInput with its own table and sends its rumble to Sony's library (scePadSetVibration). The library it ships (2017) opens only a USB DualShock 4, so the rumble reaches a DualSense only when the pad is shown to the game as one.
games.libraryNote: Its input is read through DirectInput.
games.description: With the pad shown as a DualShock 4 the game's Sony library opens it and the game rumbles it, on a cable and over Bluetooth. Shown as a DualSense it plays with the right controls and PlayStation prompts but never vibrates.
games.settings: Game Feel: the pad shown as a DualShock 4 (patch 0013, in MacGameFix 1.5.6 and later). Steam Input off.
details: Shown as a DualShock 4, the game's library read the pad's reports 0x12, 0xa3 and 0x02 and set 0x14, all answered by the modules, then wrote the DualShock 4's output 0x05 with its motors; the modules turned it into the DualSense's.
With the Edge shown as a DualSense, XInput off, on the motors or as a controller, the game sent no vibration request at all.
No light bar write was seen in the session.

tests.notes: XInput off, with Steam Input still on for the game. Controls and PlayStation prompts right.
XInput's rumble on the motors, Steam Input off: no vibration request reached the modules in 3 minutes.
The pad also as an XInput controller, Steam Input off: still no vibration request.
Vibrated (the user); 34 motor rises in the log, up to 0xff.
Vibrated (the user); 13 motor rises in the log, both motors up to 0xff.
Vibrated (the user); 40 motor rises in the log, up to 0xff.

games.name: Crash Bandicoot 4: It's About Time
games.technology: Unreal Engine 4.24. It reads an XInput controller, and a DualShock 4 with its own code over HID: shown as one, the game reads the pad's DualShock 4 reports itself and rumbles it.
games.description: Shown as a DualShock 4 it shows PlayStation buttons and rumbles the motors. As an XInput controller it rumbles too, with Xbox buttons; the game lets you choose its button prompts in its own settings.
games.settings: Game Feel: the pad shown as a DualShock 4, XInput off. Steam Input off.
details: Shown as a DualShock 4, the game read the DualShock 4's feature reports 0x12 and 0xa3, answered by the modules, then wrote its motors itself: 16 rises in two and a half minutes, up to 0xe6.
As an XInput controller it rumbled through XInput, with Xbox button prompts: 41 rises in four minutes.

tests.notes: As an XInput controller: vibrates (the user), Xbox prompts; 41 motor rises through XInput.
PlayStation prompts and vibration (the user); 16 motor rises, written by the game to the DualShock 4.

games.name: Crash Bandicoot N. Sane Trilogy
games.technology: Vicarious Visions' engine. It reads XInput and DirectInput, and rumbles only an XInput controller. A DualShock 4 seen through DirectInput is its PS4 controller type, with PlayStation prompts, but it never rumbles one.
games.description: As an XInput controller it rumbles, with Xbox button prompts; the game has no setting for its prompts. Shown as a DualShock 4 it shows PlayStation buttons and does not vibrate. Which one is the player's choice: vibration as an XInput controller (the setting kept here), or PlayStation buttons as a DualShock 4.
games.settings: Game Feel: the pad as an XInput controller (by the store's rule). Steam Input off. For PlayStation buttons without vibration: the pad shown as a DualShock 4.
details: Shown as a DualShock 4 the controls and the PlayStation prompts were right, and the game sent no vibration at all: none to the pad, and none to XInput's rumble on the motors, which the modules had ready beside it.
Its executable classifies controllers (ECONTROLLERTYPE_PS4) and imports only XInputGetState and XInputSetState from XInput, so it cannot see a Sony pad behind XInput.

tests.notes: As an XInput controller: vibrates (the user), Xbox prompts; 834 motor rises in five minutes through XInput.
XInput off: PlayStation prompts, no vibration request in the log.
XInput's rumble on the motors beside it: PlayStation prompts, and still no vibration request.

games.name: God of War Ragnarök
games.technology: Its executable carries Sony's library (libScePad: adaptive triggers, haptics) and loads it through the PlayStation PC SDK, but under Wine Steam answers that it runs on a Steam Deck, and the game never loads the SDK. What is left is XInput.
games.description: As an XInput controller it rumbles on the motors, with Xbox button prompts and no adaptive triggers or haptics: those come from Sony's SDK, which does not run under Wine.
games.settings: Game Feel: the pad as an XInput controller, set for the game (the store lists the DualSense). Steam Input off.
details: 347 motor rises in three minutes, up to 0xc9 on both motors, through XInput.
Under NotProton, Steam's IsSteamRunningOnSteamDeck answers yes, so the game skips PsPcSdk and libScePad; told no, the SDK's initialisation fails (0x8a800111) and the game exits (measured 2026-10-16).

tests.notes: Vibrates well (the user); Xbox prompts, no adaptive triggers.
